:::{#def-big-omega}
#### Big-Omega notation

For $f$ and $g$ as in @def-big-o,
we write $f(n) = \Omega(g(n))$ if there are a constant $c > 0$
and an integer $n_0$ such that

$$f(n) \ge c \, g(n) \quad \text{for every } n \ge n_0.$$

Dividing by $c$ shows that this holds exactly when $g(n) = O(f(n))$,
with constant $1/c$.

:::
